conceptZh: 科學家老鼠輕輕推倒一塊骨牌，彩色試管連鎖倒下，剛好排成「時」。
object: a bespectacled lab mouse with a line of dominoes made of colorful test tubes
morph: a domino chain of fizzing tubes tumbles and lands as the strokes of 時
creativeAngle: 骨牌連鎖加上準時的鬧鐘，聲音和畫面同步。
promptEn: An 8-second animated clip on a pale lilac background, with one single Traditional Chinese glyph 時 as the only text on screen, drawn in emerald green solid strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with generous margins. 0-1.7s: a round-eyed lab mouse in a white coat and thick glasses pokes the first test-tube domino with a pencil while a beaker fizzes over on cue; the first 時 is spoken as the sun-shaped left 日 tube tips and lands upright. 1.7-3.4s: the chain rattles across a lab bench, a wobbling beaker hiccups bubbles, one tube spins in place before falling; second 時 as the 土 and 寸 tubes click down beside the 日. 3.4-5s: 準時 is spoken as a toy alarm clock at the end of the chain rings exactly when the last tube lands, the mouse's glasses sliding down in surprise, then pushing them back up. 5-8s: hold; the glyph rests still while the mouse takes a bow and a bubble floats up. Audio: a warm off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "時、時、準時" (ㄕˊ、ㄕˊ、ㄓㄨㄣˇ ㄕˊ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between the two single utterances, and stops after the word; no other speech, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Final 3 seconds (5-8s): the glyph 時 is perfectly still and fully readable while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. Bright but not neon palette, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing.

conceptZh: 大怪獸在滑溜溜的地板上助跑、趴下來像保齡球一樣肚皮滑行，第一次滑太短只碰倒一根球瓶，第二次整排十根藍色球瓶被撞飛，翻滾落地剛好排成「時」，發條鯊魚咬錯東西一口咬下大鬧鐘按鈕，鈴聲剛好準時響起。
object: a huge round fuzzy one-horned cartoon monster belly-sliding like a bowling ball into a row of ten tall cobalt-blue bowling pins, while a chunky wind-up toy shark guards a big round toy alarm clock at the end of the lane
morph: the ten knocked-over pins tumble, spin and land flat as the ten solid strokes of 時: four pins stack into the 日 box on the left, three settle as 土 on the upper right and three as 寸 on the lower right, locking into clean solid strokes
creativeAngle: 上一版是科學家老鼠推骨牌，這次改成全新的「肚皮滑行保齡球」實體笑料：大怪獸的笨拙個性（一轉身就撞倒東西）直接變成撞倒球瓶的動力，十根球瓶對應「時」的十筆，撞擊本身就排出字形。發條鯊魚負責「咬錯東西」咬到鬧鐘按鈕，讓「準時」在鈴聲響起的那一刻被看見，聲音與畫面一致。
promptEn:
An 8-second 2D-style animated clip on a pale butter-yellow background with a glossy, slippery pastel floor. The only text ever on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 時, built from ten tall cobalt-blue bowling pins that land as solid, clean strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with generous margins.

0-1.5s: A huge round fuzzy orange monster with one stubby horn and a goofy grin stands at the far left, staring at a neat row of ten cobalt-blue bowling pins in the center. It rubs its belly, points at the pins, and does a big tiptoe wind-up, tail wagging. At the far right a chunky wind-up toy shark stands beside a big round toy alarm clock, chomping at the air. The first 時 is spoken as the monster lunges forward.

1.5-3s: The miss. The monster flops onto its belly too early and spins slowly like a plate, sliding to a stop just short of the row. Its nose boops the first pin, which only wobbles. The shark darts in and bites the wobbling pin instead of anything useful, lets go, and spins once in a circle on the floor.

3-4.5s: The big one. The monster backs up until it fills the left edge, pounds its feet, charges right, dives and slides belly-first across the floor like a bowling ball with a long squash-and-stretch. CRASH: all ten pins fly up, tumble and spin in the air, then clack down one by one into place. Four pins stack into the 日 box on the left, three settle as 土 on the upper right, and three as 寸 on the lower right, locking into the solid cobalt-blue glyph 時. The second 時 is spoken exactly as the last pin clicks down.

4.5-5.8s: The shark, still chomping at the wrong things, bites the alarm clock's big button; the bell rings and the clock hops, exactly as the monster pops up from its slide with a dizzy grin. 準時 is spoken over that ringing moment, the glyph fully formed and readable in the center.

5-8s: Final hold. The glyph 時 stays perfectly still and fully readable. Below and to the sides, away from the strokes, the monster strikes a wobbly bowling strike pose, then does a tiny happy hip-wiggle, while the shark finishes one slow spin and bumps gently against the clock.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly 時、時、準時 (ㄕˊ、ㄕˊ、ㄓㄨㄣˇ ㄕˊ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between the two single characters, and stops after the word. Soft cartoon slide and clack sounds, a gentle clock bell, no background music louder than the voice, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Bright but not neon colors, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing.
